original_question: Develop and study new geometric properties of tilings, analogous to bounded-displacement equivalence, bi-Lipschitz equivalence, or similar geometric notions, that are invariant under mutual local derivability, topological conjugacy, or homeomorphism.
target_in_paper: Problem 2.7.2 in §2.7.1, “Properties of Patterns and Properties of Tiling Spaces” (p. 588): develop and study new geometric properties, analogous but not identical to BD, BL, etc., that are invariant under MLD, topological conjugacy, or homeomorphism. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies that the problem is about creating new geometric properties for tilings, modeled on BD/BL-type notions, and requiring invariance under MLD, topological conjugacy, or homeomorphism. It also correctly aims at the open-ended development problem itself, rather than the neighboring classification problem in Problem 2.7.1. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
missing_details: The paper explicitly says the new properties should be “analogous but not identical” to BD, BL, etc.; your draft omits the paper-critical phrase “but not identical.” ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

The nearby motivation in §2.7.1 is to reconcile two viewpoints: geometric questions about individual patterns/tilings (BD, BL, LR, diffraction, Meyer property) and dynamical/topological questions about tiling spaces (cohomology, maximal equicontinuous torus, dynamical spectrum). Making that motivation explicit keeps the question faithful to the paper rather than turning it into a generic metric-geometry prompt. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

For a stand-alone formulation, the abbreviations should be expanded at least once: BD = bounded displacement, BL = bi-Lipschitz, MLD = mutually locally derivable. The Introduction supplies these definitions, and LR is part of the nearby motivating list even though Problem 2.7.2 itself mentions only BD, BL, etc. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

The intended invariance should be made explicit: if two tilings are related by MLD, or if their tiling spaces are topologically conjugate or homeomorphic in the sense discussed in §2.7.1, then the property should hold for one exactly when it holds for the other. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

The paper frames this as a “more ambitious (and open-ended) challenge” following Problem 2.7.1, not as a request to classify already-known invariant properties. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

No ambient ring, field, operator, homogeneity/degree restriction, nilpotency assumption, or ‘for all sufficiently large m’ quantifier appears here; this is a qualitative tiling-theory problem, so importing such data would be unfaithful to the paper. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
refined_question: Can one develop and study new geometric properties of tilings or patterns—analogous, but not identical, to bounded-displacement (BD), bi-Lipschitz (BL), and related geometric notions—such that these properties are invariant under mutual local derivability (MLD) and under topological conjugacy or homeomorphism of the associated tiling spaces, in the sense that equivalent tilings share the property? ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
justification: The draft matches Problem 2.7.2 almost verbatim, so that is the nearest official formulation and the right target. The surrounding paragraph in §2.7.1 explains exactly why this problem is posed: geometric properties of specific patterns (such as BD, BL, LR, pure point diffraction, Meyer property) are often not preserved under the equivalence relations that make tiling spaces dynamically/topologically ‘the same,’ namely MLD, topological conjugacy, and sometimes homeomorphism. Problem 2.7.1 first asks for strong versions of existing properties that survive these equivalences; Problem 2.7.2 then asks the broader follow-up captured by your draft: to formulate genuinely new geometric properties with that invariance. The Introduction provides the meanings of BD, BL, LR, and MLD that are needed to make the question stand alone. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
